title: Customs Amendment (Singapore-Australia Free Trade Agreement Amendment Implementation) Bill 2017
short_title: Customs Amendment (Singapore-Australia Free Trade Agreement Amendment Implementation) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would update Australian customs law to reflect changes to the free trade agreement with Singapore.
It would create new rules for deciding which goods from Singapore qualify for lower tariffs, and set out how to claim that treatment.
The new rules would replace the existing framework after a three-year transition period, and the changes would start on the later of royal assent or the amendment agreement's entry into force.
changes: Introduce new rules of origin for goods imported from Singapore.
Introduce new procedures for claiming preferential tariff treatment for Singaporean originating goods.
Extend record keeping obligations for Australian originating goods exported to Singapore.
summary.affected: Importers and exporters of goods between Australia and Singapore.

divisions.question: The majority voted in favour of the bills' main idea. In parliamentary jargon, they voted to read the bills for a [second time](https://www.peo.gov.au/learning/fact-sheets/making-a-law.html). ### What is the main idea of the bills? The bills make the changes *"necessary as a result of recently agreed changes to the rules of origin in the [Singapore‑Australia Free Trade Agreement](http://dfat.gov.au/trade/agreements/safta/Pages/singapore-australia-fta.aspx) (SAFTA)"*. Read more in the [bills digest](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/bd/bd1718a/18bd041).

speeches.speaker: Steven Ciobo
speeches.brief: The bill implements amendments to the Customs Act to give effect to the updated Singapore-Australia Free Trade Agreement, which serves as the economic pillar of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership announced in June 2015. The changes introduce simplified rules of origin, improve market access for services such as law and financial services, and build on an 80% increase in bilateral trade and 350% rise in investment since the original 2003 agreement.

speeches.speaker: Steven Ciobo
speeches.brief: The speaker moved the second reading of the Customs Tariff Amendment (Singapore-Australia Free Trade Agreement Amendment Implementation) Bill 2017, which amends the Customs Tariff Act to implement the amended agreement by providing duty-free access for most eligible goods, adjusting concessional items, and inserting a new schedule for excise-equivalent rates on alcohol, tobacco, and fuel, with a three-year transition period before repealing the old provisions.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Customs Amendment (Singapore-Australia Free Trade Agreement Amendment Implementation) Bill 2017 and cognate bill, but criticised the Turnbull government for waiving labour market testing for contractual service suppliers and for a lack of transparency and independent economic modelling. The two-way trade between Australia and Singapore was valued at $22.7 billion in 2016.

speeches.speaker: Ian Goodenough
speeches.brief: The Customs Amendment Bill introduces new product-specific rules of origin and self-certification to simplify administration and reduce compliance costs for traders under the Singapore-Australia Free Trade Agreement. The upgraded agreement also includes mutual recognition of professional qualifications, a raised Foreign Investment Review Board screening threshold to $1,094 million for private Singaporean investment, and new visa arrangements for longer stays.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: The Customs Amendment (Singapore-Australia Free Trade Agreement Amendment Implementation) Bill 2017 was supported, with Singapore’s free trade success contrasted against Venezuela’s economic collapse (460% inflation, -8% growth, 21,000 murders) to argue for the agreement’s benefits in education, legal accreditation, and financial services.

speeches.speaker: Nola Marino
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Customs Amendment Bill for the Singapore-Australia Free Trade Agreement, highlighting tariff removal and market access for goods and services from their south-west Western Australia electorate, including wine, lamb, beef, marron, abalone, chocolate, olive oil, cheeses, and fudge, as well as opportunities for education, irrigation, and professional services via the upgraded Busselton-Margaret River Airport.

speeches.speaker: Jason Clare
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Customs Amendment and Customs Tariff Amendment bills to implement the second update to the Singapore-Australia Free Trade Agreement, which provides duty-free access for most goods, updates rules of origin, restricts ISDS mechanisms with public welfare exemptions, and recognises Australian qualifications. However, Labor opposed the removal of labour market testing for contractual service suppliers, arguing it contradicts the government's earlier commitment to mandatory testing.

speeches.speaker: Steven Ciobo
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Customs Amendment bills to implement the updated Singapore-Australia Free Trade Agreement (SAFTA), citing $4.8 billion in services exports to Singapore in 2016 and criticizing the member for Herbert for not contributing to the debate on the deal's benefits for Townsville.
